CANNON-RECOIL-STARBOARD — Braced wide-legged at the starboard gun-deck, his shoulder slammed against the brass breech as the sky-cannon kicks backward mid-fire, smoke erupting from the muzzle in a billowing grey wall, a spent shell spinning past his boot, coat-tails whipping in the recoil-blast, the enemy frigate's hull filling the smoke beyond — the next round is already in his hand.

BOARDING-LEAP — Launching from the gunwale mid-dogfight, both ships barely ten feet apart, a brass pistol extended in his right hand and a cutlass trailing in his left, coat streaming horizontal, cannon-flash from below lighting his face copper, the enemy deck rushing up to meet his boots in the next heartbeat.

CUTLASS-PARRY-GUNWALE — Twisted hard at the waist on the port-side gunwale, both arms raised to catch a sky-cutlass blow, sparks cascading where the blades grind together, his free hand white-knuckled on the brass railing, an enemy boarder already pivoting for a second swing, the open sky wheeling behind them both.

SPEAKING-TUBE-COMMAND — Bent over the chart-table on the bridge with his lips pressed to a brass speaking-tube, one fist driving a divider point into the course-line, amber gauge-light rippling across his face, the ship shuddering under him from a cannon-hit — his next exhaled word will change the heading by forty degrees.

SPYGLASS-HELM — Gripping the ship's wheel with his left hand, body canted forward into the slipstream, a brass spyglass raised to his eye with his right, coat snapping hard against his arm, the horizon alive with enemy signal-smoke — in one second he will spin the wheel hard to starboard.

RIGGING-STORM-REPAIR — Halfway up the portside rigging in driving rain, knees hooked over a ratline, a brass wrench clenched between his teeth, gauntleted hands yanking a torn fin-brace back into its housing, lightning forking white across the dirigible-spine directly behind him — the brace will either seat or snap in the next pull.

SWINGING-RIGGING-LEAP — Mid-swing on a hawser-line between the two locked ships, body fully suspended above the gap, a cutlass raised in his free hand, both vessels' gun-smoke rising around him, rope burning through his gauntlet, coat billowing open — his boots will slam the enemy crow's nest platform in under a second.

SIGNAL-FLARE-GUNWALE — Standing at the port-rail with his arm thrown fully overhead, a brass-handled flare pistol just fired, the red-smoke corkscrew still tight and climbing, the muzzle-bloom fading orange against his face, coat snapping sideways in the altitude-wind — his eyes are already tracking whether the allied ship has seen the signal.

VORTEX-PROW-STAND — Planted feet-wide on the bowsprit platform as the airship noses into a vortex-spiral, coat streaming straight back in a rigid banner, both hands locked on the prow-rail's brass stanchions, cloud-wall spinning ahead in a grey-green churn — the ship's nose will plunge another thirty degrees in the next second.

ASTROLABE-CLOUD-DECK — Leaning back against the observation-railing on the navigation-deck, astrolabe held at arm's length toward a break in the overcast, fingers adjusting the alidade ring, the reading-lamp behind him swinging on its gimbal in the turbulence, coat pressed flat against his ribs by the upwelling wind — the fix will either confirm or contradict the dead-reckoning.

ENGINE-VALVE-CRISIS — Torso wedged into the engine-room housing between two brass manifolds, both hands wrapped around a misfiring pressure-valve, steam jetting white past his ear, sweat and condensation streaking his face, the deck vibrating with a terminal shudder — one more quarter-turn and the valve either seals or bursts.

PISTOL-FIRE-BOARDER — Body twisted mid-step on the gun-deck gangway, a brass pistol discharged point-blank at a boarder mid-leap from the rail, muzzle-flash blooming between them, smoke obscuring the boarder's face, his own arm recoiling back toward his shoulder — he is already reaching for the second pistol at his hip.

SPOTTER-PLATFORM-SWEEP — Leaning far out from the spotter-platform high in the upper rigging, one arm hooked through the brass safety-bar, a spyglass extended into the slipstream, coat-tails fully horizontal and snapping, the main-deck a toy-size rectangle far below — his grip will tighten as the enemy formation comes into focus.

HAWSER-HAUL-LISTING — Thrown back against the severe cant of the listing deck, hauling hand-over-hand on a braided hawser rigged to the counterweight-spar, boots scrabbling on oil-dark planking, rain sheeting horizontal past his silhouette, every tendon in his neck taut — the ship will either answer the pull or roll another five degrees.

CANNON-FUSE-LIGHTING — Crouched low beside the forward cannon on the gun-deck, a brass match-striker sparking in his cupped hands, the cannon's fuse-port open and waiting, an enemy hull enormous in the gun-port beyond, his coat pooled behind him in the crouch — in two seconds the gun will fire and the recoil will throw him aside.

SPAR-SPRINT-CUTLASS — Running the full length of the upper spar above the envelope, arms out for balance, a cutlass raised in his right hand, an enemy grapple-crew scrambling toward him from the far end, wind tearing at his coat, the ground-level sky vertigo-far below — the gap between them will close in four running strides.

SIGNAL-LANTERN-COMMAND — Hanging one-handed off the signal-bracket on the bridge-wing, brass signal-lantern swinging in the other hand, his body cantilevered out over the open air to catch the sightline of the allied ship ahead, coat billowing open, the lantern's shutter clacking through a coded sequence — the reply flash has just appeared on the distant hull.

CLOCKWORK-BIRD-RELEASE — Braced at the stern-rail in the slipstream, both hands opening to launch a clockwork messenger-bird, its brass wings already blurring to speed, a scroll-canister glinting at its belly, his coat shoved back from the wing-downwash — he is already looking toward the target ship to watch for its arrival.

DIVING-PROW-CLING — Flattened against the prow-housing as the airship noses into a steep dive, arms locked around the brass figurehead-brace, feet lifted off the deck by the acceleration, coat pressed flat to his back then flaring at the hem, the cloud-cover rushing upward past him — the next second will either level the dive or steepen it.

CHART-BRASS-QUILL — Bent hard over the navigation-table in the chart-room below the bridge, a brass-tipped quill dragging a new course-line across the vellum chart, his other hand holding down the curling edge, gas-lit gauges glowing amber in a row behind him, the ship yawing slightly under a wind-shear — the line will reach the new waypoint marker in one more stroke.

ENEMY-DECK-LANDING — One boot already on the enemy gunwale, the other still clearing the gap, body low and forward, a cutlass sweeping wide for balance and threat, cannon-smoke from the enemy's own guns rolling past him, coat trailing like a flag — the enemy crew in the smoke ahead has just registered his arrival.

SPEAKING-TUBE-BROADSIDE — Gripping the helm-rail with one fist, the other arm fully extended with a brass speaking-tube pressed to his mouth, mid-shout, the entire ship heeling under a broadside impact, gauge-panels flickering amber to red behind him, his body thrown sideways by the list — the word in the tube is a firing order.

FIN-BRACE-RIGGING-CRISIS — Both feet on a storm-jostled ratline halfway up the starboard-fin mast, one arm hooked over the spar, the other driving a brass coupling-pin into a split fin-brace with the heel of his palm, sparks jumping from the metal-on-metal contact, the dirigible-envelope bulging and thrashing a foot from his shoulder — the pin needs one more strike to seat.

PISTOL-RECOIL-FLARE-RECON — Kneeling on the observation-sponson above the engine-nacelle, one arm braced on the brass housing, a flare-pistol just fired straight up, wrist jolted back by recoil, the green-smoke trail corkscrewing overhead, his eyes already tilted skyward tracking the signal — an allied silhouette has appeared in the cloud-break directly above.

WHEEL-BROADSIDE-HOLD — Both hands locked on the helm-wheel's brass spokes, torso leaning forward into it, coat blasted flat against his back by a near-miss cannon-shock, the wheel fighting him as the rudder bites, gas-lamp behind him swinging violently on its gimbal — the ship's bow is swinging two degrees per second toward the gap in the enemy line.

STARBOARD-CANNON-RECOIL — Braced wide-legged on the gun-deck as the starboard sky-cannon kicks back against his shoulder, brass breech slamming into his chest-rig, smoke billowing from the muzzle in a dirty white cloud, a spent shell spinning past his boot, coat-tails whipping in the recoil-blast, an enemy frigate materializing through the haze a hundred yards off the port bow, the next shot already being rammed home behind him.

BOARDING-LEAP-MID-GAP — Airborne between the Esperanza's gunwale and the enemy deck, cutlass raised in his right hand and a brass flintlock in his left, coat streaming fully horizontal, the cloud-floor visible six hundred feet below through the gap, cannon-flash from the lower deck lighting him orange from beneath, his boot one second from striking the enemy rail.

CHART-TABLE-COMMAND — Leaning hard over the bridge chart-table, one gauntleted fist on the brass speaking-tube shouting course corrections, the other hand still gripping a brass divider mid-measure, amber gas-gauges glowing behind him, wind screaming through the shattered forward porthole, the helmsman already spinning the wheel hard to starboard in response.

SPYGLASS-SPOTTER-PLATFORM — Leaning hard into the slipstream from the high spotter-platform, brass spyglass pressed to his eye, coat-tails blown fully horizontal, one boot hooked behind the platform rail for purchase, the deck a dizzy forty feet below, an enemy formation just resolving in the eyepiece, his free hand already reaching for the signal-lantern at his hip.

HAWSER-HAULING-LIST — Body thrown nearly horizontal against the cant of the listing deck, both fists hauling hand-over-hand on a braided hawser lashed to the portside ballast-winch, boots scrabbling on oil-dark planking, rain sheeting horizontally past, the ship groaning as it begins to answer, a second crewman sliding into him from behind to add their weight.

SWINGING-RIGGING-BETWEEN-SHIPS — Caught mid-arc on a rigging-line between two locked ships, left hand gripping the block-and-tackle, cutlass in his right trailing sparks where it scraped the enemy hull, both boots clearing the void, the boarding-rope fraying above him under his weight, the enemy deck rising fast to meet him.

SPEAKING-TUBE-WHEEL-BRIDGE — Gripping the ship's wheel hard with both hands while a brass spyglass is wedged under his arm, shouting the bearing change to the engine-room through the speaking-tube clenched in his teeth, the bridge windows streaked with rain, the altimeter needle spinning down behind him, his knuckles white on the wheel as the ship begins to respond.

ASTROLABE-CLOUD-READING — Pressed against the navigation alcove rail with the astrolabe raised at arm's length against a break in the cloud-cover, the brass instrument catching amber reflected light from the gas-envelopes, his other hand scrawling a reading into the chart-ledger, the ship bucking in the updraft, the pencil line going jagged across the page as another gust hits.

ENGINE-VALVE-WRENCH — Both hands wrenching a misfiring pressure-valve in the engine-room, back arched against the resistance, a jet of superheated steam screaming past his cheek from a cracked fitting inches to his left, the brass pressure-gauge behind him spiking into the red, sparks dripping from a shorted cable overhead, the valve beginning to turn just as the deck shudders with a second detonation.

BOW-DIVE-CLINGING — Flattened against the prow with both arms locked around the brass bowsprit-ring, the ship pitching into a forty-degree dive through a storm-vortex, coat plastered flat against his body by the wind, hair and coat-collar streaming straight up behind him, cloud rushing past in white streaks, the ship's altitude-horn screaming somewhere behind him.

PISTOL-BOARDER-MUZZLE-FLASH — Standing at the head of the companionway with a brass pistol extended at arm's length, muzzle-flash blooming white in the dimness, a boarder mid-leap on the stairs directly below the barrel, powder-smoke rolling back across his face, a second pistol already clearing his belt with his left hand, the hit boarder's body still mid-fall.

FIN-CLIMB-MID-STORM — Three-quarters of the way up the dirigible's dorsal fin-strut in full storm, one boot hooked around the strut-cable, the other dangling free as the ship rolls, his gauntleted hand slapping a brass patch-plate over the torn fabric and hammering it with a mallet, rain streaming off his shoulders, the fin-fabric tearing further twelve inches above the patch.

COURSE-PLOTTING-GAUGES — Bent hard over the navigation desk, brass quill tracing a new course-line across the chart as three gas-lit pressure-gauges glow amber behind him, his other hand spinning a parallel-rule to check the bearing, the desk lamp swinging on its gimbal from turbulence, the chart's edge fluttering under his elbow, the heading already half-drawn when the ship yaws.

ENEMY-DECK-FIRST-STEP — One boot just touching the enemy deck and the second still clearing the rail, body in full forward lean, brass pistol already discharging into a knot of defenders, muzzle-flash lighting his face, the cutlass swinging back for a follow-through cut, the gap between the two ships yawning behind him where he cannot retreat, the fight already beginning around his first footfall.

VORTEX-BOW-STANDING — Standing upright on the narrowing bowsprit platform as the ship drives through a cloud-vortex, both arms spread for balance, coat streaming straight back, the brass bowsprit-lamp beside him extinguished by the wind, the vortex wall rotating in grey and white thirty meters ahead, altitude dropping fast on the gauge behind him, his weight shifting forward onto his toes as if to meet it.

ROPE-RIGHTING-RAIN — Both boots braced against a deck-cleat on the listing starboard rail, body nearly parallel to the tilted planking, hauling a braided rope lashed to the emergency ballast-dump lever, rain hammering the envelope above, the ship groaning as the ballast shifts, the horizon beginning to level in the gap between the clouds ahead, a second heave already loading in his shoulders.

HORIZON-SWEEP-SLIPSTREAM — Leaning a full shoulder into the slipstream from the forward spotter-platform, one arm hooked around the brass platform-stanchion, the other sweeping the cloud-horizon with a long brass spyglass, coat-collar cracking in the wind, a faint silhouette just resolving at the glass's limit, his free hand already releasing the stanchion to reach for the signal-lantern clipped to the rail below.

TOPSIDE-CANNON-SECOND-SHOT — Ramming a fresh charge into the topside swivel-cannon with a brass-tipped rammer, knees bent against the deck-roll, coat-tails streaming in the blast-wind from the previous shot still visible as dissipating smoke, the enemy envelope looming directly overhead at a hundred feet, powder grains spilling from the cartridge across the dark planking, the rammer clearing the muzzle one second before the next command to fire.

BOARDING-LEAP-GUNWALE — Launching from the port gunwale with a cutlass raised and a brass pistol leveled, coat fully horizontal behind him, the cloud-gap between the two ships yawning below his boots, cannon-flash from beneath lighting his jaw, enemy deck rushing up to meet him.

RIGGING-REPAIR-STORM — Climbing the dirigible-spine rigging mid-squall, a brass wrench clenched in his teeth, one gauntleted fist locked around a rain-slick cable, the torn stabilizer fin flapping at his shoulder, lightning strobing the envelope above, the next handhold just out of reach.

SPYGLASS-HORIZON-PLATFORM — Leaning hard into the slipstream from the spotter-platform at the top of the forward mast, one boot lifted off the grating, brass spyglass pressed to his eye, coat-tails streaming fully horizontal, the gun-deck a small rectangle far below, a dark shape resolving in the clouds ahead.

WHEEL-COMMAND-BRIDGE — Hauling the ship's wheel hard to port on the command bridge, a brass spyglass tucked under his arm and his coat straining across the shoulder, gas-lit gauges spiking amber behind him, the bow shadow swinging through the window, the helmsman bracing for the next order.

SPEAKING-TUBE-CHART-TABLE — Shouting into the brass speaking-tube bent over the chart-table on the bridge, a brass divider still pressed to the chart in his free hand, amber gauge-light painting his face, a penciled arc of the new course half-finished beneath his fingers, the helmsman's acknowledgment crackle audible.

ASTROLABE-CLOUD-COVER — Pressing an astrolabe to his eye on the open navigation-deck, one elbow braced on the brass sighting rail, cloud-cover shredding just enough to expose a star, coat lifting in the thermal updraft, his other hand poised with a brass quill over the log-book for the instant the angle locks.

PROW-DIVE-CLINGING — Clutching the prow figurehead brace as the ship pitches nose-down into a cloud-dive, body nearly horizontal behind the bowsprit, coat tearing backward in the rush of cold air, knuckles white on the brass fitting, the cloud wall swallowing the bow a second away from total white-out.

PISTOL-BOARDER-MID-LEAP — Firing a brass flintlock pistol point-blank at an enemy boarder in mid-leap over the starboard railing, muzzle-flash lighting both their faces, the recoil snapping his wrist back, his own body already pivoting to bring the cutlass in his left hand forward for whoever lands behind.

FIN-REPAIR-LIGHTNING — Wrapped around the upper steering-fin brace in the rigging, one arm hooked through the cable and the other driving a brass bolt home with a mallet, the torn canvas panel cracking against his chest, lightning forking past the envelope two ship-lengths away, the next hammer-blow still mid-swing.

MESSENGER-BIRD-RELEASE — Standing at the aft gondola hatch with a clockwork messenger-bird launched from his open palm, the brass wings already blurring, his fingers still curled from the release, coat swept back by the prop-wash, eyes tracking the bird's wobbling trajectory toward the allied ship vanishing into cloud.

VORTEX-BOWSPRIT — Standing on the bowsprit brace as the ship enters an atmospheric vortex, arms spread for balance, coat torn straight behind him in a perfect horizontal stream, cloud-walls spiraling in his peripheral vision, his next move either a grab for the forestay or a free-fall into white turbulence.

RIGGING-HAUL-STORM — Hauling a mainsheet rope hand-over-hand from the mid-deck cleat during a full storm, feet spread and heels dug into the planking, rain driving sideways across his face, the rope burning through his gauntlets as the gas-envelope strains above, the next pull required before the gust overwhelms him.

RECON-SPYGLASS-CLOUDBANK — Braced against the forward rigging shroud on the observation platform, spyglass extended at full length toward a cloudbank on the port quarter, one boot hooked around a ratline, slipstream pulling at his collar and cuffs, the dark silhouette inside the cloud just sharp enough to be a hull.

BROADSIDE-RECOIL-STAGGER — Staggered one step backward on the gun-deck by the full broadside recoil, one hand catching a deck-ring to keep upright, smoke flooding the gun-bay, brass shell casings rolling past his boots, the enemy ship's responding muzzle-flashes already visible through the smoke thirty yards off the beam.

FLINTLOCK-AT-BOARDERS — Arm fully extended over the starboard railing, brass pistol bucking in his fist mid-discharge, muzzle-flash illuminating the face of a boarder caught mid-leap across the gap, his coat snapping back from the report, the second boarder behind the first already raising a cutlass.

SKY-CUTLASS-PARRY — Blades locked at eye-level on the gunwale, his back heel hanging off the edge over open sky, the crossed steel throwing a fan of orange sparks against his collar, his free hand white-knuckled on a brass stay-wire, the enemy boarder leaning his full weight into the bind — the next strike is already cocking behind the boarder's shoulder.

SECOND-CUTLASS-RIPOSTE — Pivoting on the gun-deck mid-riposte, wrist torquing the sky-cutlass in a tight arc after a parry, his leading boot sliding an inch on oil-dark planking, coat-tail sweeping outward with the rotation, sparks still drifting from the preceding clash, the boarder's balance broken backward toward the railing.

PISTOL-RELOAD-BOARDERS — Biting the paper cartridge with his back teeth at the gun-deck rail, powder hand already tilting toward the pan, a spent boarder crumpled behind him on the planking, another swinging in over the railing on a grapple-rope, the ship yawing so the horizon tilts beyond the attacker's shoulder.

GUNWALE-LEAP — Both feet leaving the starboard gunwale in full extension, brass pistol cocked forward in his right hand, cutlass raised in his left, the gap between the two ships a vertical corridor of smoke and cannon-flash below him, his coat streaming horizontal, the enemy deck rushing up beneath his boots.

RIGGING-SWING-BETWEEN-SHIPS — Body arcing on a hemp rigging-line between the two hulls, free hand on the cutlass hilt, the rope bowing deep at the apex of the swing, enemy deck planking rising fast below, both ships' cannon-smoke braiding together around him, his boots about to connect with the enemy's foredeck railing.

SPAR-SPRINT — Running the length of the horizontal spar above the main-deck with a cutlass raised overhead, the wood creaking under his stride, coat horizontal in the slipstream, an enemy crewman at the far end raising a pistol, the dirigible envelope vast and grey above, the deck a narrow stripe of oak below.

GRAPPLE-HOOK-BOARDING — Swinging the brass-capped grapple hook in a full overhead rotation from the bow, body torqued back, coat whipping forward with the release, the hook already arcing toward the enemy rail trailing its line through cannon-smoke, his other hand already gripping the rope to follow it across the gap.

WHEEL-AND-SPYGLASS — Both hands not quite matching — right hand white-knuckled on a spoke of the great brass helm, left arm raised with the spyglass extended toward the forward window, coat-collar up in the cockpit wind, the compass-rose spinning beneath his palm, a second ship's silhouette hardening in the glass ahead.

SHOUTING-ORDERS-BROADSIDE — Leaning out over the bridge railing through an open port, one hand cupped at his mouth, the other gripping the brass frame of the port, cannon-smoke from the broadside rolling up past his face, his coat pressed flat against his chest by the hot gases, the gun-crews below already pivoting for the next volley.

CHART-TABLE-COURSE-PLOT — Bent over the illuminated chart-table at a sharp angle, brass quill scratching a new heading as the compass needle swings, the gauges behind him glowing amber and green, one boot lifted slightly as the deck pitches, his free hand pressing the chart's edge flat, the altitude-gauge needle climbing past the red mark.

SPYGLASS-FROM-SPOTTER-PLATFORM — Leaning hard into the slipstream from the spotter-platform high in the rigging, one arm hooked around the brass mast-ring, spyglass extended full-length into the wind, coat-tails streaming completely horizontal, the deck a narrow strip far below, the cloud-bank ahead beginning to resolve into an enemy fleet's silhouettes.

ASTROLABE-IN-CLOUD-COVER — Braced against the fin-strut above the navigation deck, both arms raised, the brass astrolabe held at arm's length against a break in the cloud-cover, fingers adjusting the alidade, wind tearing his coat open, the horizon tilted thirty degrees in the gap, his eyes narrowed on the arc-scale, course-correction imminent.

STORM-RIGGING-REPAIR — Halfway up the port-side rigging in the storm, one arm looped through the rope-ladder, the other driving a brass wrench onto a sheared fin-bolt, lightning forking white past the dirigible-spine behind him, rain sheeting diagonally across his face, the torn fin-panel thrashing loose two rungs above his head.

LISTING-SHIP-HAWSER-HAUL — Body thrown back against the deck's full thirty-degree cant, hauling hand-over-hand on a braided hawser lashed to the collapsed port ballast-winch, boots skidding on oil-dark planking, rain sheeting past at an angle, every tendon in his neck visible with the effort, the ship's cant beginning — barely — to ease.

MISFIRING-ENGINE-STRIKE — Striking the jammed ignition-hammer of the portside engine with a brass mallet, the blow still at its apex, sparks showering from the contact point, steam venting sideways across his shins, the engine coughing into an uneven idle, the whole propeller-assembly vibrating through the decking under his boots.

SIGNAL-FLARE-LAUNCH — Arm raised to full extension at the gunwale, brass-handled flare-pistol discharging, the flare already corkscrewing skyward trailing a tight helix of red smoke past his raised fist, his coat snapping back from the report, head tilted upward tracking the flare, the distant allied ship still dark on the horizon ahead.

CLOCKWORK-MESSENGER-BIRD — Arm fully extended off the port-rail at shoulder height, brass clockwork messenger-bird at the moment of release, its gear-wings already blurring into motion, a tiny burst of compressed-air vapor at his wrist from the launch-spring, his fingers still open from the release, the bird banking away into the cloud-layer above the enemy formation.

FUSE-LIGHTING — Crouching at the cannon's touch-hole on the gun-deck, brass match held to the fuse as the cord catches in a spitting orange curl, his other hand bracing the carriage against the pre-fire vibration, the enemy hull filling the gunport behind him, one heartbeat before the world goes white with muzzle-flash.

SPYGLASS-HORIZON — Leaning into the slipstream from the spotter-platform high in the rigging, a brass spyglass pressed to his eye, coat-tails streaming fully horizontal, one boot hooked behind a ratline for purchase, the ship's deck a toy far below, a distant smear of smoke on the horizon locked in the lens, his free hand already reaching for the signal-flag clipped to his belt.

RIGGING-LINE-SWING — Mid-arc on a braided rigging-line between the two ships, body curled to clear the gap, cutlass raised in his free hand, wind tearing at his collar, the enemy ship's deck rushing into view below, the rope at its apex of swing, the moment before his boots hit the enemy rail.

VALVE-WRENCH-CRISIS — Straddling a burst steam-pipe in the engine compartment, both hands wrenching a misfiring brass valve counter-clockwise, a geyser of white steam screaming past his right ear, goggles fogged, boot braced against the pipe-housing for leverage, the needle on the pressure-gauge behind him buried in the red, the ship's whole frame shuddering around him.

HAWSER-HAUL — Body thrown backward against the cant of the listing deck, hauling hand-over-hand on a braided hawser coiled through a brass block, boots braced and sliding on oil-dark planking, rain sheeting diagonally past him, every muscle in his arms and back taut against the ship's weight, the deck-angle fractionally, grudgingly beginning to right.

ASTROLABE-READING — Perched on the lip of the navigation-alcove with one knee up, holding a brass astrolabe at arm's length against a break in the cloud-cover, lips moving in calculation, a pencil tucked behind his ear, the ship rolling gently under him, a stripe of cold white moonlight catching the instrument's graduated arc, the chart on the table behind him still blank of their true position.

BOARDER-PISTOL-MID-LEAP — Firing a brass pistol at an enemy boarder mid-leap across the gun-deck, arm fully extended, muzzle-flash blooming, body still in the air from the jump, coat-tails lagging behind him, smoke biting at his eyes, the boarder already stumbling back against the railing, a second man vaulting over him from the enemy ship beyond.

BOW-VORTEX-STAND — Standing spread-legged on the bowsprit platform inside the edge of a cloud-vortex, coat shredded horizontal by the rotational wind, one arm raised to shield his eyes from debris, the vortex wall a moving grey mass ten yards off the starboard bow, the ship's figurehead vibrating against the pressure, his hair and collar tearing forward as the ship punches through.

COURSE-PLOT-MID-CRISIS — Dragging a brass quill across the chart-table in a hard arc, his other hand splayed on the chart to hold it against the ship's roll, three glowing amber gauges casting orange rings on his face, a speaking-tube receiver swinging loose and knocking the inkwell, the quill-line not yet complete, the heading he is drawing converging on a gap marked in red.

ENGINE-ROPE-HAUL — Climbing hand-over-hand up an engine-room rope-pulley system with his feet walking the curved hull-wall, a wrench jammed in his belt clanking against the rivets, steam rising from a burst coupling below him, sparks showering from a sheared gear-housing to his left, the rope fraying one strand at a time above his highest grip, the engine's irregular knock telling him he is almost out of time.

ENEMY-DECK-BOARDING — One boot landing on the enemy ship's rail and one still in the air behind him, a cutlass already sweeping forward in a horizontal arc, brass pistol smoking from the shot he fired during the leap, coat billowing in the gap-wind between the two hulls, the enemy helmsman lunging toward him, the two ships grinding together with a sound like thunder.

SPEAKING-TUBE-FIRE-ORDER — Slammed sideways against the bridge railing by a near-hit concussion, speaking-tube still jammed to his lips, mouth open mid-shout of a fire-order, coat smouldering at the shoulder from debris, smoke rolling through the bridge windows, the compass-binnacle knocked loose and spinning at his feet, the next broadside still forming in his throat.

FIN-CABLE-EMERGENCY — One arm hooked around the dirigible's tail-fin strut in high wind, body swinging free of the hull, a brass cable-clamp in his other hand mid-attachment to the broken fin-stay, the fin-panel drumming against his back, the ship below him canted fifteen degrees in a storm-roll, rain horizontal, the unclipped end of the cable whipping past his face like a lash.

FLARE-PISTOL-RECON — Crouched at the edge of the observation-gondola hatch, arm extended outward into the slipstream, a brass flare-pistol firing a green flare that arcs downward into the cloud-layer below, illuminating the shadowed silhouette of an enemy ship lurking beneath the overcast, his coat billowing back into the gondola interior, his eyes locked on the shape now emerging in the green light, hand already moving to the speaking-tube.

PISTOL-FIRE-AT-BOARDERS — Arm fully extended over the gunwale railing, brass flintlock pistol mid-discharge, muzzle-flash scorching his cuff, a boarding enemy caught mid-leap between the two hulls below, the recoil already rolling his wrist back and his free hand already reaching for the cutlass at his hip.

CUTLASS-PARRY-ON-GUNWALE — Both blades locked at eye-level, sparks cascading off the crossed steel, his back boot braced on the brass gunwale cap to absorb the strike, free hand gripping a rigging-line for balance, the enemy boarder's second arm already swinging wide for a follow blow he hasn't yet seen.

FUSE-LIGHTING-MID-BATTERY — Crouching at the cannon's touch-hole, brass match-case open in his fist and the lit match-cord grazing the fuse, one eye closed against the coming flash, the gun-crew ducking away behind him, powder-smoke already threading upward, the cannon about to speak in the next half-second.

SECOND-CUTLASS-PRESS — Driving a sky-cutlass two-handed into a pressed parry against an enemy officer on the port-side gun deck, knees bent low for leverage, boot grinding on a spent shell casing, sparks raining from the locked blades, the enemy beginning to fold backward toward the open rail and the long drop beyond.

BRASS-PISTOL-VOLLEY-REPEL — Half-turned on the main deck companionway stairs, firing a second brass pistol downward at a boarding party swarming up through the hatch, muzzle-flash lighting the smoke-filled stair from above, his elbow against the frame for stability, spent pistol already dropping from his other hand to free it for the blade.

GUNWALE-LEAP-ONTO-ENEMY-DECK — Airborne in the gap between two hulls, both ships trading cannon-fire beneath him, a brass pistol in his right hand and a cutlass in the left, coat fully horizontal in the rush of wind, the enemy deck's railing two feet ahead, cannon-flash from below lighting his silhouette against the smoke.

SPAR-SPRINT-CUTLASS-RAISED — Running the full length of the starboard lower-spar toward the enemy's grappled hull, cutlass raised overhead and boot-tips barely kissing the timber, wind tearing his collar open, the spar flexing under his weight, three enemy sailors bracing to receive the charge at the spar's far end one stride away.

BOARDING-LINE-RELEASE — Standing on the gunwale cap, one hand releasing a brass-cleated grappling-line as his body tips forward into the leap, coat billowing behind him, the gap between the two hulls opening below like a chimney of smoke and fire, his leading foot already committed to the enemy deck coming up fast.

SPEAKING-TUBE-ORDERS — Bent over the chart-table on the bridge, lips pressed to the brass speaking-tube horn, a brass divider gripped white-knuckled in his other hand mid-gesture over the course-chart, gas-lit amber gauges flickering behind him in the storm-light, his next order already half-formed and the helmsman's acknowledgment bell beginning to ring.

SHOUTING-THROUGH-STORM-BRIDGE — Gripping the bridge rail with one gauntleted hand and turning full into the gale to bellow at the deck crew below, the brass speaking-tube swinging free on its chain, rain sheeting horizontally across his face, his other arm cutting a sharp command-gesture downward, the crew already scrambling toward the threatened stern-fin.

COURSE-PLOTTING-UNDER-FIRE — Pinning a course-chart to the navigation table with one brass-gauntleted forearm while dragging a brass quill across it in a sharp new heading, the gauges behind him glowing amber and one cracked and hissing steam, the ship canting five degrees to starboard mid-stroke and sending the ink-pot sliding toward the edge.

RIGGING-REPAIR-MID-STORM — Halfway up the dirigible-spine rigging, both legs wound around the ratline and a brass wrench gripped in his teeth, gauntleted hands forcing a split fin-strut back toward its mounting bracket, lightning forking white behind the gas-envelope above him, the torn canvas fin cracking like a gunshot in the gale and threatening to pull the bracket free entirely.

STORM-RIGGING-LASH — Clinging one-armed to the outer rigging on the port side in full storm, the other arm driving a marlinspike through a failing rope-lash to resecure a flailing gas-valve cover, the cover slamming against his shoulder with each gust, lightning throwing his shadow twice across the envelope above him, the lash three half-hitches from holding.

SIGNAL-FLARE-PISTOL — Arm raised vertical at the starboard-quarter gunwale, a heavy brass-handled flare-pistol at full extension, the flare already clear of the muzzle and corkscrewing skyward trailing a coiling thread of red smoke, the recoil rolling his wrist back toward his ear, his other hand shielding his eyes upward to confirm the trajectory through the overcast.

CLOCKWORK-MESSENGER-RELEASE — Standing at the aft-deck railing into the headwind, both hands cupped around a brass clockwork messenger-bird as its wings begin their first rapid stroke, the mechanism whirring audibly, the bird's gyroscope spinning up with a rising tone, his fingers opening to release it, the bird already angling away on its locked heading into the grey sky ahead.

BOARDER-PISTOL-VOLLEY — Braced in a wide stance on the portside gunwale, he fires a brass flintlock pistol at an incoming boarder mid-leap, the muzzle-flash lighting his jaw from below, spent powder scorching his glove, the enemy swinging on a rigging-line toward him — a second later the gap between ships will close.

CUTLASS-PARRY-RAILING — He catches a sky-cutlass blow with his own blade at the brass guardrail of the main deck, sparks cascading across the rail, his free gauntlet pressed flat against the railing for leverage, the attacker's momentum driving both men sideways — a knee-strike is already loading in his rear leg.

BOARDING-LEAP-ACROSS — He launches from the gunwale with a cutlass raised and a brass pistol cocked in his off-hand, the gap between both ships yawning beneath him, cannon-flash from the lower gun-deck lighting his coat from below, his boots trailing above the void — the enemy deck rushes up fast.

RIGGING-SWING-CUTLASS — Swinging hard on a braided rigging-line strung between two ships locked in broadside combat, he reaches full arc over open sky, cutlass extended in his free hand, the line vibrating at peak tension, coat fully horizontal — his boots will hit the enemy crow's nest in under a second.

FUSE-LIGHTING-CROUCH — Crouched low at the brass cannon's touch-hole on the lower gun-deck, he presses a glowing match-cord to the fuse, sparks hissing along the powder-train, his other hand shielding his face from the coming flash, body torqued sideways to clear the recoil — the cannon is already beginning to thunder.

SPAR-SPRINT-RAISED-BLADE — Sprinting the length of the main spar with a cutlass raised overhead, the boom swaying beneath his boots, rigging-lines whipping past his shoulders, coat tearing in the wind, the enemy's deck mast rushing toward him — he'll be on the enemy helmsman in three more strides.

WHEEL-GRIP-SPYGLASS — Gripping the helm's brass wheel with one hand during a hard climbing turn, he holds a spyglass to his eye with the other, the deck tilted fifteen degrees under his planted boots, a flanking enemy ship sliding into the glass's field — his mouth is already opening to call the new bearing.

SIGNAL-LANTERN-BRIDGE — Standing at the bridge's aft railing, he pumps a brass signal-lantern in a rapid coded sequence toward a sister-ship half a kilometer off, the lantern's beam cutting through rain-haze, his free arm braced on the rail against the ship's roll — the reply-flash from across the dark is just starting to blink back.

ASTROLABE-CLOUD-READ — Standing at the navigator's alcove on the mid-deck, he holds a brass astrolabe up to a break in the cloud-cover, eye squinted along the sighting arm, the ship banking gently around him, gauges glowing amber at his back — his free hand is already moving to annotate the chart.

BRASS-QUILL-COURSE-PLOT — Hunched over the illuminated chart-table in the navigation bay, he drags a brass-tipped quill along a new course-line as altitude gauges glow green beside him, his free hand anchoring the chart against the ship's vibration — the heading he's drawing curves directly into the storm-cell ahead.

HAWSER-HAUL-LIST — Hauling hand-over-hand on a braided hawser to drag the listing ship back to trim, his whole body thrown backward against the deck's cant, boots grinding against oil-slick planking, rain sheeting horizontally past him — another hand is about to grab the line two feet behind him.

TORN-SAIL-ALOFT — Clinging to a cross-spar thirty meters above the main deck, he pulls a flapping canvas panel back against the frame with one hand while his other lashes it with a short length of rope, the gas-bag swaying massively above him, wind screaming through the rigging — one knot more and the sail will hold.

PROW-DIVE-CLING — Gripping the prow-rail with both hands as the airship pitches into a steep downward run, his body nearly horizontal behind him, coat streaming straight back like a flag, boots barely hooked over the bowsprit bracket, the cloud-layer rushing up — the altimeter on the binnacle behind him is spinning counterclockwise.

CLOCKWORK-BIRD-LAUNCH — Standing at the aft rail of the command deck, he releases a clockwork messenger-bird from both palms, its brass wings already spinning to full-beat, the small machine climbing steeply against a grey sky, wind pulling his coat forward — he watches it for one second before turning back to the helm.

SECOND-CANNON-BROADSIDE — At the mid-deck battery during a rolling broadside exchange, he steps back from a recoiling gun as smoke swallows the port side, grabs the next powder-cartridge from the hoist with his free hand, ears ringing, coat grey with powder-dust — he's already pivoting back to ram the charge home.

SPEAKING-TUBE-PURSUIT — Running along the starboard walkway during a pursuit turn, he presses a brass deck-phone to his mouth without breaking stride, calling speed orders down to engineering, his free arm out for balance as the ship heels, rigging lines slapping past his shoulder — the engine telegraph is still ringing behind him.

CANNON-FUSE-BROADSIDE-CROUCH — Crouched beneath the recoiling carriage of the aft sky-cannon as it fires above him, a brass lighter still smoking in his fist from lighting the touch-hole, the concussion flattening his coat against his back, a shell-casing ringing off the deck beside him — he's already rising to sight the next shot himself.

SPYGLASS-HORIZON-SWEEP — Leaning hard into the slipstream from the spotter-platform high in the rigging, a brass spyglass extended and pressed to one eye, coat-tails streaming dead horizontal behind him, the deck a small oil-lamp scatter far below, his free hand white-knuckled on the platform rail as he tracks something moving fast through the cloud-bank ahead.

BRASS-PISTOL-MIDLEAP-BOARDERS — Firing a brass flintlock pistol at point-blank range at a boarder who has just cleared the rail, the muzzle-flash blooming white between them, recoil snapping his wrist upward, his own body still in mid-step backward along the gangway, a second boarder visible on the rail beyond the smoke already swinging a boarding-axe.

WHEEL-COMMAND-SPYGLASS — Gripping the ship's brass wheel with both hands while a spyglass is wedged under his arm, shouting a bearing over his shoulder, the wheel fighting him in a crosswind that tilts the deck five degrees, gauges flickering amber on the curved bridge-glass ahead of him, his knuckles white on the spoke as the ship answers.

BOW-PROW-DIVE — Gripping the prow-figurehead mount with both hands as the ship noses sharply downward into a dive, body nearly horizontal, boots hooked under the bowsprit-brace behind him, the cloud-layer rushing up at his face, coat streaming directly upward past his ears, the altimeter on his wrist-strap spinning visibly as he rides the plunge.

COURSE-PLOT-BRASS-QUILL — Leaning over the navigation table with a brass-nib quill mid-stroke across the vellum chart, the other hand splayed on the compass-rose for reference, amber engine-gauges glowing behind him through the brass-framed porthole, a new heading emerging line by line, already glancing up at the clouded sky beyond the glass for confirmation.

VORTEX-BOW-STAND — Standing wide-legged on the bowsprit platform as the ship drives into a cloud-vortex, one hand death-gripped on the forestay, coat streaming straight back and snapping in the rotational wind, the vortex wall curving around him in green-grey cloud, the ship's brass prow-light flickering in the electrical charge, the eye of the vortex a clear second away.

ENGINE-CLIMB-TORN-FIN — Halfway up the port-side engine-nacelle strut in mid-storm with a brass ratchet-strap looped over his shoulder, one hand gripping a rivet-bar and one boot finding a cooling-louver for a step, the torn fin clanging against the strut above him, rain driving horizontally past the gas-bag, his next grip a slick brass handhold a body-length overhead.

ENEMY-DECK-LAND — Hitting the enemy quarterdeck in a forward stumble off his boarding-leap, cutlass already sweeping horizontal at chest height, his coat still billowing upward from the drop, one knee bent to absorb the landing, the rigging-line trailing behind him still, two enemy crew members spinning away from the cutlass arc before he has fully stopped moving.

ROPE-HAUL-RIGHTING — Throwing his whole weight backward against a rain-soaked deck-rope at the waist-cleat of the main gas-envelope, hands raw on the braid, boots leaving dark drag-marks on the tilting deck, the envelope straining against its torn anchor-ring above him, a second crewman not yet in frame whose rope he is compensating for with every muscle locked.

SPOTTER-PLATFORM-SIGNAL — Braced on the highest spotter-platform against the rigging-mast, firing a brass signal-pistol upward at a steep angle, the muzzle-flash bright against the grey overcast, smoke immediately shredded sideways by altitude wind, his other hand locked on the mast-ring, the deck and gas-envelope both visible far below as he tracks the flare's climb.

PARRY-AND-ADVANCE-BOARDING — Catching a second boarder's blade in a high parry at the top of the boarding-ramp, stepping forward into the bind rather than back, sparks cascading down onto the brass deck-grating between their boots, his free hand closing on the boarder's coat-lapel to drag him off-balance, a third shape swinging in over the rail a breath behind.

FIN-REPAIR-STORM — Halfway up the port-side rigging in howling crosswind, a brass wrench clamped in his teeth and a rope looped twice around his gauntleted forearm, body wrenched sideways by a gust as lightning forks past the dirigible-spine behind him, his free hand slapping at the torn fin-canvas — next second he drives the first bolt home.

RIGGING-SWING — Mid-arc on a hawser swinging between his own ship's foremast and the enemy's topside rail, knees bent to absorb the landing, a cutlass raised high, slipstream tearing his coat open wide, the two hulls grinding in the gap below — next second his boots crack onto the enemy rail and the blade descends.

SPYGLASS-PLATFORM — Leaning hard into the forward slipstream from the spotter-platform high in the rigging, a brass spyglass pressed to his eye, his free hand locked on the shroud, coat-tails streaming fully horizontal, the main deck tiny below, a distant ship resolving in the lens — next second he snaps the glass shut and shouts the bearing down.

PISTOL-BOARDER — Planting his rear boot on the brass railing mid-recoil, arm extended in the follow-through of a shot, muzzle-flash still blooming at the barrel's tip, grey powder-smoke curling back across his face, a boarder mid-leap in the background — next second he swings the pistol butt as a club and draws his cutlass.

VALVE-WRENCH — Straddling the engine-housing deep in the engineering bay, both hands wrenching a brass valve counter-clockwise with every gram of his weight, steam screaming from the flange around it, goggles misted white, sparks cascading off the adjacent gear-train onto his shoulder — next second the valve gives and pressure drops with a thunderclap hiss.

SIGNAL-FLARE — Arm fully extended upward at the port gunwale, a brass-handled flare-pistol in his fist at the moment of discharge, the flare corkscrewing skyward in a tight red helix trailing crimson smoke, the recoil rolling his shoulder back, his other hand gripping the railing — next second an answering flare blooms on the horizon.

CANNON-FUSE — Crouching at the breech of the bow-chaser, a brass match-holder in his right hand, the lit end touching the fuse with smoke already curling upward, his left forearm raised to shield his face, the fuse hissing, the target ship framed dead-centre through the open bow-port — next second the cannon erupts and the deck shakes.

WHEEL-GRIP — Both hands locked on the helm's brass spokes as the ship heels in a hard-port turn, a spyglass tucked under his right arm, body leaning into the spin, the deck falling away at a steep angle behind him, rigging singing under strain overhead — next second he calls out the new heading and the guns realign.

CUTLASS-PARRY — Weight dropped into a low brace on the starboard gunwale, cutlass raised vertically to catch a descending boarder's blade, sparks spraying where the steel meets, his free hand flat on the brass railing for leverage, a second enemy swinging in from the rigging — next second he shoves off the parry and thrusts.

PROW-CLING — Chest pressed to the figurehead-brace at the very prow, both arms locked around the brass bowsprit fitting, coat streaming straight back, the ship nosing into a steep dive through cloud, condensation whipping past his face in white streaks, the ground visible far below — next second the ship levels out and he hauls himself upright.

COURSE-PLOTTING — Hunched over the navigation table mid-roll, brass quill pressed to the chart at the moment ink meets paper, his other hand bracing a parallel-rule against the ship's pitch, amber gauges glowing on every side, smoke drifting in from the deck above — next second he barks the new heading into the speaking-tube at his elbow.

ENGINE-CLIMB — Halfway up the interior engine-ladder mid-crisis, one hand gripping the rung above, the other swinging a brass mallet at a seized drive-shaft coupling, sparks ricocheting off the housing onto his coat, steam roaring from a fractured pipe beside him — next second the coupling breaks free and the shaft begins to turn.

SIGNAL-LANTERN — Leaning out over the bridge-rail with a brass signal-lantern held at arm's length, clicking the shutter in short-long-short bursts, wind tugging the amber beam sideways, coat ballooning behind him, the answering ship's lantern winking back through the murk — next second he turns and relays the message in a sharp shout.

VORTEX-BOWSTAND — Standing wide-legged on the bow-walkway inside a full rotary vortex, one hand locked on the brass stay, coat shredding sideways in competing wind-currents, cloud-debris spiralling past his face, the ship's nose oscillating five degrees either side of true — next second he shouts a trim-order and the stabilisers bite.

RIGGING-REPAIR-LEAN — Body suspended nearly horizontal from the upper-yard, one boot hooked in the ratlines for purchase, both hands feeding a splice-clamp around a snapped shroud-cable, coat flapping in machine-gun bursts, the deck far below tilting in the storm-swell — next second the clamp bites and the tension returns to the line.

PISTOL-SALVO-RECOIL — Sideways-braced on the amidships rail, arm thrown back in full pistol-recoil, muzzle-smoke drifting across his face, a boarder stumbling at mid-ship, three more climbing the hull-cleats behind the first — next second he tosses the spent pistol aside and his hand finds the cutlass grip.

BOARDING-LINE-SWING — At the lowest arc of a rigging-line swing between hulls, knees bent and coat streaming vertical, a brass-handled boarding axe in his free hand already targeting the enemy's rail-cleat, cannon-flash from below throwing hard shadows — next second he releases the line and drops the two feet to the enemy deck.

ENEMY-DECK-FIRST-STRIKE — Boots just landing on the enemy's amidships planking in a running crouch, cutlass already mid-swing at waist height, his own ship's hull visible over his shoulder, the gap between the two ships closing fast, smoke from the last broadside drifting through the scene — next second the blade connects and the counter-attack begins.

GUNWALE-PARRY — Weight thrown back on his left boot along the brass-railed gunwale, a cutlass crossed hard against an enemy blade, sparks showering from the contact point, his free hand gripping the railing to stay aboard, the attacker's second arm already swinging for a follow strike; the rigging hums with tension above him.

SIGNAL-FLARE-FIRE — Standing at the starboard gunwale with one arm punched skyward, a brass-handled flare pistol just fired, the flare corkscrewing upward trailing a coil of red smoke above his fist, coat snapping hard to port in the crosswind; the answering ship on the far ridge of cloud has not yet seen it.

SWINGING-BETWEEN-SHIPS — Mid-arc on a rigging-line between two hulls, one hand locked above him on the iron ring, cutlass extended forward in the other, boots clear of both decks with open sky beneath, the enemy ship's rigging rushing toward him, smoke from a broadside still hanging in the gap between hulls.

MISFIRING-VALVE-WRENCH — Crouched on the engine-room catwalk with both hands torquing a brass pressure-valve that is sheeting live steam past his shoulder, coat pinned against his back by the jet, face turned aside, sparks raining from a cracked conduit above him; the gauge needle is still climbing into the red arc.

WHEEL-GRIP-COMMAND — Planted at the helm with both hands locked on the spoked brass wheel mid-hard-turn, a spyglass tucked under his other arm, his coat billowing forward from the speed-dive, the bridge glass fogging with condensation; the enemy broadside is already visible as orange light through the forward viewport.

SPRINTING-THE-SPAR — Running full stride along a horizontal spar with a cutlass raised, the deck and open sky alternating below each step, his free arm thrown out for balance, coat-tails lifting behind him, an enemy boarder at the far end raising a pistol; another step and the blades will meet.

PISTOL-AT-BOARDERS — Firing a brass pistol point-blank at a boarder mid-leap over the rail, the muzzle-flash lighting both their faces, recoil kicking the gun back past his ear, his coat-sleeve scorched at the cuff, a second boarder already visible on the rope behind the first; the shot has not yet found its mark.

ENEMY-DECK-SPRINT — Five strides across an enemy deck mid-boarding, cutlass forward, the gap between the two ships still visible at his back, enemy crew rising from cover ahead, smoke from a cannon-discharge rolling across the planking at boot-level; his sword arm is already drawing back for the first engagement.

ENGINE-CONDUIT-CLIMB — Halfway up a vertical engine-room conduit ladder with a brass gear-tool hooked to his belt, sparks showering from a fractured pipe above, steam-pressure bowing the conduit wall outward, his knuckles white on the rung, coat-hem caught in the updraft; the rupture point is three rungs above his next handhold.

TORN-FIN-CABLE-HAUL — Hanging from the envelope's lower-spine rigging with both feet hooked in a rope-loop, hauling a snapped fin-cable back toward its cleat, the wind tearing the slack cable like a whip, his coat pressed flat against his chest, the storm-lit horizon tilted ninety degrees below him; the cleat is one pull away.

BROADSIDE-RELOADING-RUN — Sprinting along the gun-deck mid-reload with a brass powder-cartridge cradled against his chest, smoke thick at knee-height from the last salvo, a cannon-crew reaching toward him from the nearest gun-port, empty brass casings skittering underfoot; the enemy ship's shadow is crossing the gun-ports in sequence as it rakes their course.

RIGGING-LINE-SWING-PURSUIT — Mid-swing on a starboard rigging-line carrying him from the mainspar toward a fleeing enemy sloop, one hand locked above on the iron shackle, a boarding-hook ready in the other, the sloop's taffrail rushing at him through the smoke, wind pulling his coat-tails up like wings; the hook is already swinging forward to catch.

HORIZON-SWEEP — Leaning hard into the slipstream from the spotter-platform high in the rigging, one arm hooked around the rope-stay, brass spyglass pressed to his eye, coat-tails streaming fully horizontal, the deck a small rectangle of brass and shadow far below — his free hand is rising to adjust the focus-ring.

RIGGING-SWING-TRANSFER — Mid-swing between two ships on a single rope-line, body arced back, cutlass raised in his free hand, clouds rushing past behind him, the enemy's rigging approaching fast, a cannon-ball tearing the air a yard from his shoulder — his legs are swinging forward to absorb the impact of landing.

PISTOL-BOARDER-FIRE — Firing a brass flintlock pistol at a boarder mid-leap toward him on the gun-deck, the muzzle-flash a white-orange disc inches from the boarder's coat, recoil snapping his own arm upward, smoke punching forward, the spent flint spinning free — his free hand is already reaching for the second pistol at his hip.

FLARE-PISTOL-SIGNAL — Standing at the gunwale with a brass-handled flare pistol raised overhead, the flare already corkscrewing skyward on a corkscrew trail of red-orange smoke, his coat snapping horizontal in the slipstream, the rail vibrating under his other hand — the flare is at apex before its parachute deploys.

WHEEL-AND-GLASS — Gripping the brass ship's wheel with both hands except for the spyglass jammed under his chin, banking hard into a turn, deck canting, gas-lit instruments blurring behind him, the lens catching a distant ship's profile — his fingers are already hauling the port spoke down.

FIN-CABLE-HAUL-STORM — Clinging to the upper envelope-rail in a full gale, both hands hauling a snapped fin-cable back through its brass cleat, the cable tearing at his gauntlets, lightning silhouetting the entire dirigible-frame behind him, the fin itself flapping like a broken wing — one more pull and the cleat will catch.

COURSE-PLOT-CRISIS — Leaning hard over the chart-table with a brass quill dragging a course-correction across the vellum, gauges behind him glowing amber and red simultaneously, his other hand flat on the chart to hold it against the ship's roll, ink blotting from the sudden lurch — his head is already turning to the altitude-dial.

BROADSIDE-RELOAD-RACE — Ramming a powder-charge home on the gun-deck cannon mid-broadside, one knee on the deck, both arms driving the ramrod, muzzle-smoke from the last shot still eddying around him, an enemy hull broadside-on in the port gap — the touch-hole is a second from being primed.

RIGGING-LIGHTNING-CLIMB — Three-quarters up the mainmast ratlines in full storm, left arm hooked through the rungs, right arm reaching for the next rope, lightning striking the lightning-rod above him in a white branching crack, the shockwave pressing his coat flat to his body — his right hand closes on the next rung.

SIGNAL-PLATFORM-SCAN — Pressed against the signal-platform railing at the dorsal fin-base with a brass spyglass extended, body angled into the wind, the ship banking beneath him so the horizon tilts across the lens, vapor streaming off the envelope above — his free hand is raising to tap a recognition-code on the signal-lantern shutter.

CANNON-RECOIL STARBOARD — Braced wide-legged on the gun-deck, both hands locked on the brass breech as the sky-cannon kicks back hard against his shoulder, smoke erupting in a fat grey ring from the muzzle, a spent shell spinning bright at his boots, the enemy frigate filling the porthole beyond; he is already dragging a fresh charge from the rack.

BOARDER-PISTOL MID-LEAP — Airborne over the gap between two locked ships, a brass flintlock leveled in his right hand at a boarder mid-leap from the opposite gunwale, coat streaming horizontal, muzzle-flash painting his face amber, cannon-smoke churning below him; the cutlass in his left hand is already rising for the landing.

CUTLASS-PARRY ON THE RAIL — Twisted hard at the waist on the port gunwale, both wrists catching an enemy sky-cutlass on his own blade, sparks sheeting off the locked steel, his free gauntlet braced against the brass railing to hold his footing, coat rucked up by the impact; the boarder's second hand is already reaching for his belt-knife.

FUSE-LIGHTING CROUCH — Crouched low at the base of the aft sky-cannon, a brass match hissing in his fingers inches from the fuse, his other arm thrown up to shield his face from the anticipated flash, powder-smoke already threading from the touch-hole, the deck vibrating with a previous broadside; the fuse tip is just catching.

GUNWALE-LEAP TO ENEMY DECK — One boot leaving the gunwale cap-rail, the other already clearing it, a cutlass raised in his right hand and his coat peeling back off his shoulder in the wind-shear between the two ships, cannon-flash from the enemy deck lighting him from below; his feet will hit their planking in under a second.

RIGGING-SWING BETWEEN SHIPS — Halfway along a rigging-line strung between two running ships, both hands gripping the brass block-fitting, body swinging in a long arc above the cloud-gap, boots kicking forward for momentum, coat-tails streaming back past his hips; the enemy ship's rail is rushing up to meet him through the smoke.

SPAR-SPRINT RAISED CUTLASS — Running the length of a horizontal spar above the main deck at full tilt, left arm thrown out for balance, cutlass raised high in his right, boot-heels sparking off the brass spar-fittings, wind tearing his collar open; two decks below an enemy boarding-party has just looked up and seen him coming.

SPEAKING-TUBE COMMAND — Bent over the brass chart-table on the bridge, mouth pressed to the speaking-tube trumpet with a shout that pulls his neck tight, a brass divider gripped in his free hand still touching a plotted course-line, amber gauges flaring at his back, the ship rolling under him; his knuckles are whitening on the divider for the next correction.

WHEEL-GRIP WITH SPYGLASS — Both hands on the great brass wheel, legs braced against a hard-banking turn, a half-open spyglass clamped between his right palm and a spoke, his gaze cutting out the forward bridge-glass at a distant contact, coat-collar blown back against his jaw; the wheel is still turning under the pressure of his grip.

SIGNAL-LANTERN SWING — Standing at the bridge-wing railing with a brass signal-lantern held high and swinging in a deliberate arc, his other hand gripping a stay-cable to hold position in the slipstream, coat snapping rigid behind him, the lantern's shutter throwing a bar of amber light across low cloud; the answering flash from the distant ship has not yet come.

SHOUTED BEARING — Leaning out over the bridge-rail to shout a bearing to the helmsman below, one hand cupped around his mouth, the other arm hooked hard around a brass stanchion, the ship banking so steeply the cloud-layer is visible directly beneath his hanging boots; the helmsman's hand is already moving to the wheel below.

CHART-COURSE PLOTTING — Hunched over the illuminated navigation-table in the chart-room beneath the bridge, a brass quill scratching a hard course-correction across the vellum, the compass-gauges and altitude-dials glowing green and amber around him, his other hand pressing the chart flat against the table's pitch, ink still wet on the last mark; his eyes have already jumped to the next waypoint.

SPYGLASS SPOTTER-PLATFORM — Leaning into the full slipstream from the spotter-platform high in the envelope-rigging, a brass spyglass pressed to his eye, both legs hooked through the platform cables for anchorage, coat-tails blown fully horizontal and snapping, the main deck a small rectangle far below; he is already reaching for the signal-flag at his belt.

ASTROLABE CLOUD-READ — Standing on the forward observation-deck with an astrolabe raised to eye-level in both hands, tilting it against a gap in the cloud-cover, feet spread wide on the pitching deck, coat pushed back by the headwind, the brass instrument catching a sliver of starlight; his lips are moving with the calculation and his free fingers are already reaching for the notebook.

STORM-RIGGING REPAIR — Climbing the dirigible's port-spine rigging mid-storm, a brass wrench gripped between his teeth, one arm looped through a rope hitch for anchorage, the torn fin canvas whipping past his face with a crack, lightning forking behind the envelope above him; his free hand is reaching for the flapping fin-spar.

HAWSER-HAUL TO RIGHT THE SHIP — Body thrown sharply backward with the cant of a listing deck, hauling hand-over-hand on a braided hawser attached to the starboard ballast-spar, boots braced against an oil-dark cleat, rain sheeting horizontal past his face, the rope burning through his gauntlets; the deck angle is fractionally beginning to ease under his effort.

MISFIRING VALVE WRENCH — Jammed into the narrow engine-access corridor beneath the propulsion deck, both hands torquing a brass pressure-valve that is venting live steam past his shoulder, goggles pulled down, jaw set against the heat, the corridor walls shaking with misfiring engine-beats; the valve is just starting to give under his weight.

FIN-SPAR LASHING MID-GALE — Straddling the dirigible's upper tail-fin spar in full gale, knees clamped to the spar, leaning out to lash a fractured support-strut with a length of copper cable, wind tearing the cable from his grip, the envelope roaring above him; the next gust is already darkening the cloud-face behind the ship.

ENGINE-ROOM ROPE-HAUL — Standing in the engine-room hatchway, legs spread over the pitch of the deck, hauling a jammed drive-belt back onto its flywheel with a looped rope, sparks spitting from the spinning brass rim, the belt smoking where it drags, sweat cutting through the grease on his face; the flywheel is three inches from seating.

PROW-DIVE CLINGING — Spread-eagled on the bowsprit as the airship pitches nose-down into a steep dive, fingers locked around the brass prow-fitting, boots skidding on the curved hull-plating, coat blown forward over his head so only his goggles are clear, the cloud-layer rushing up to swallow the bow; his grip is the only thing between him and a long fall.

BOW-VORTEX STAND — Standing upright at the very tip of the bow-deck with both arms thrown wide for balance as the ship enters a pressure-vortex, coat fully inverted and streaming forward past his face, the air column visible as a darkening spiral ahead, boots magnetized to the brass deck-rail by sheer will; the ship is already beginning to yaw inside the vortex.

SIGNAL-FLARE PISTOL — Standing at the port gunwale with a brass signal-pistol raised directly overhead, arm fully extended, the flare just clearing the barrel and corkscrewing skyward trailing a hard coil of red smoke, his coat-tail blown back by the discharge, free hand gripping the rail; in the next second the flare will burst and the allied ship two miles out will see it.

CLOCKWORK BIRD RELEASE — Leaning out from the rigging-platform with one arm extended, the brass clockwork messenger-bird perched on his gauntlet and just launching, its articulated wings snapping open mid-beat, gears audible over the wind, the target ship's bearing scratched on the message-cylinder at its chest; his fingers are still open from the release, coat-sleeve still trembling with the bird's departure.

SECOND CANNON — Slamming the brass breech-block of the midship sky-cannon closed with a gauntleted palm, legs braced in a wide stance on the gun-deck, powder-smoke from the previous shot still hanging at waist-height, his head already turning to sight along the barrel at an enemy vessel crossing the smoke; his other hand is reaching for the lanyard.

BOARDING-CUTLASS PRESS — Two paces onto an enemy deck after the leap, already inside a defender's guard, cutlass pressed chest-high and driving the man backward toward the rail, coat still settling from the crossing, his rear boot finding purchase on their unfamiliar planking, a second defender visible at the corner of the frame stepping in; his elbow is already cocking for the redirect.

WHEEL-AND-SPYGLASS COMMAND — He is planted wide-legged at the bridge helm with both hands wrenching the spoked brass wheel hard to port, a collapsed spyglass gripped in his right fist against the spoke, shouting a heading over his shoulder, amber gauge-light throwing harsh shadows across his face, the bow swinging visibly through the viewport, collision with a cloudbank imminent.

RIGGING-REPAIR MID-STORM — He is three-quarters up the main rigging spine with one arm hooked through the ratlines, body angled out against the wind, a brass wrench clenched in his teeth and a torn fin-cable whipping past his ear, lightning splitting the cloud behind the dirigible-spine, his free hand reaching for the fraying anchor-point before the next gust tears it completely loose.

HAULING-THE-HAWSER — He is thrown fully backward on the canting main deck, both gauntleted hands locked on a braided hawser running up to the port-side ballast-cleat, boots sledding on oil-dark planking as the ship lists another degree, rain sheeting horizontally past the running-lights, every muscle in his back taut against the pull, the deck beginning — just barely — to level beneath him.
